Doctor Shanna Swan is an environmental health scientist whose research links chemical exposure to falling fertility and changing sexual development. On Danny Jones's podcast, she discusses the strongest form of her findings, billed as the top reason humans are suddenly being born, in the episode's word, genderless.

Swan's peer-reviewed work on phthalates and reproductive health is real and debated inside her field; the episode's framing pushes it toward its most alarming reading. Jones asks what the chemicals are, where they hide, and what parents can do. Listeners should separate her published data, which she explains carefully, from the headline built on top of it. The conversation offers a credentialed scientist's warning about plastics and reproduction, in the long form her broadcast appearances rarely allow.
podcast-dannyjones-qeF_Xcc1Dfw:
Former remote viewer David Morehouse joins Danny Jones to talk about the CIA's StarGate program. The episode title names remote viewing of Mars, Nazi occult lore, and space war. Morehouse served in the Army and in the viewer unit.

Morehouse tells how the state trained men to see far sites with mind alone. He shares tasks that ranged from hostages to Mars and the Moon. Jones asks how the unit judged hits from misses. Listeners get a spy's tale from the strangest unit in US service. The library holds the talk as an archive record of his account.
podcast-joerogan-V1-QIhvPjFw:
Comedian Tim Dillon joins Rogan in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience to discuss the UFO revelations then in the news. Dillon, a podcaster with a bleak and funny view of American life, treats disclosure as both mystery and farce. The pair's friendship drives the tone.

They sort the serious claims from the showmanship around them, laughing at the officials and marveling at the footage in the same breath. Rogan brings his years of UFO guests to bear. The segment is disclosure talk with a comic filter, useful as a record of how the news landed with two men who never stay solemn for long.
